mainEntity.name: Which Palletizer and Case Packer Fit a Typical Food Processing Line?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on line speed, product and floor space. Lower-speed, high-mix lines point to TRFCobot, limited space with more speed to TRFCompact, and high-volume or multi-line plants to TRFSpeed. For case packing, many SKUs and delicate items point to TRFRapidpack, integrated forming and sealing to TRFOnepack, and repetitive flexible bags to TRFDroppack. TRF engineering validates each application before quoting.

mainEntity.name: Can One Automation Partner Supply Palletizing, Case Packing and Conveyors for a Food Plant?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. TRF supplies case packing, conveying and palletizing as one integrated end-of-line solution: TRFRapidpack, TRFOnepack or TRFDroppack pack the cases, TRFIntraflow moves and routes them, and TRFCobot, TRFCompact or TRFSpeed build the pallet. One partner is responsible from layout to startup, and Parts and Service supports TRF-supplied equipment afterward.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Sanitary Conveyor and a Standard Industrial Conveyor?

acceptedAnswer.text: A sanitary conveyor carries exposed food and is built to be cleaned: TRFCleanflow uses open-frame construction, reduced horizontal surfaces and food-grade belting as design targets. A standard industrial conveyor such as TRFIntraflow moves packaged units (cases, cartons, trays and totes) between packing, palletizing and the warehouse. Most food plants need both, joined where the sanitation zone ends.

mainEntity.name: How Do You Choose Between a Robotic, an Integrated and a Gravity Case Packer?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with product behavior: a robotic case packer such as TRFRapidpack fits many SKUs, variable product positioning and delicate items. An integrated case packer such as TRFOnepack erects, packs and seals in one machine for smaller lines. A gravity case packer such as TRFDroppack fits repetitive flexible bags that tolerate controlled gravity loading. TRF evaluates all three for each product.

mainEntity.name: What Is the Difference Between a Dedicated Palletizing Cell and a Centralized Multi-Line System?

acceptedAnswer.text: A dedicated cell palletizes one line next to its packer. A centralized system receives cases from several lines and builds their pallets in one area. TRFSpeed scales from a dedicated cell to a centralized multi-line system, and TRFIntraflow merges, routes and accumulates the cases so the palletizer receives an organized flow. TRF validates the combined rate for each plant.

mainEntity.name: How Is Payback Estimated for Food Processing Automation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Payback depends on the labor hours the system replaces, shifts per day, local labor cost and the installed cost of the system. The estimate follows the method of the A3 (Association for Advancing Automation) robot ROI calculator: the system cost, including 20 years of maintenance at 5% per year, divided by the annual net savings, which is the labor cost of manual palletizing minus the electricity the robot uses. The palletizing ROI calculator applies this method to your location, your shifts and the people who palletize by hand today.
